title: Conservativity of base change to a separable closure
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme over a field $K$. Every geometric point of
$X$ factors through $X_{K^{\mathrm{sep}}}$, and consequently the
pullback functor along $X_{K^{\mathrm{sep}}}\to X$ is conservative: a morphism of abelian sheaves (or of derived objects) on $X_{\Et}$ is
an isomorphism if and only if its pullback to
$(X_{K^{\mathrm{sep}}})_{\Et}$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $s:X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ for the structure map, $L=K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and $p:X_L=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ for the projection. Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be any geometric point. By [def-weil-geometric-point], $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. The composite $s\circ\bar x$ corresponds, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], to a field homomorphism $a:K\to\Omega$. The extension $L/K$ is algebraic by [def-kun-separably-closed]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] to $L/K$, $\Omega$ and $a$ to obtain $b:L\to\Omega$ with $b|_K=a$. This is a choice of embedding over $K$, not an assertion that the abstract field $L$ is already a specified subfield of $\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 09GU (lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure), proof: the Zorn argument uses only algebraic closedness of the target, so applies to the algebraically closed extension Omega with the given K-structure

proof.text: Let $j=\operatorname{Spec}(b):\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. Functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $b|_K=a$ give $\operatorname{Spec}(K\hookrightarrow L)\circ j=s\circ\bar x$. The universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] therefore gives $\widetilde x=(\bar x,j):\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_L$ with $p\circ\widetilde x=\bar x$, where $X_L$ is the base change of [def-pc-base-change]. Since the domain is the same algebraically closed field, $\widetilde x$ is a geometric point. This proves the factorization clause; no uniqueness of the lift is asserted.

source.place: Tag 01JP (definition-fibre-product), universal property applied to the compatible pair (bar x, Spec b)

proof.text: Suppose $\alpha:F\to G$ is a morphism of abelian etale sheaves on $X$ and $p^{-1}\alpha$ is an isomorphism. For the lift $\widetilde x$ of any $\bar x$ just constructed, the composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition](2) gives $\widetilde x^{-1}p^{-1}\cong\bar x^{-1}$. Applying the functor $\widetilde x^{-1}$ to $p^{-1}\alpha$ preserves its inverse, so the naturality square of this comparison makes $\bar x^{-1}\alpha$ an isomorphism. By [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], this is the stalk map $\alpha_{\bar x}$, under the identification of sheaves on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with abelian groups. Since this holds for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] implies that $\alpha$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback)(3), together with Tag 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks); inverse-image composition is topologies.tex Tag 021J (lemma-composition-etale)

proof.text: For the derived clause we need composition on the entire unbounded derived category, not merely on $D^+$. The inverse images along $p$, $\widetilde x$ and $\bar x$ are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], and their derived functors are computed termwise on every complex by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], as specified in [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. On a complex $C^\bullet$, apply the sheaf comparison $c_{p,\widetilde x}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition](2) in every degree: its naturality with respect to $d^n:C^n\to C^{n+1}$ says $\bar x^{-1}(d^n)c_{C^n}=c_{C^{n+1}}\widetilde x^{-1}p^{-1}(d^n)$. Thus these components form a chain isomorphism $\widetilde x^{-1}p^{-1}C^\bullet\cong\bar x^{-1}C^\bullet$. Localizing this chain isomorphism gives the comparison of the derived functors on $QC^\bullet$. It is natural for chain maps and their homotopy classes, and hence for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms and their composites; these generate the localized morphisms. Consequently $\widetilde x_D^{-1}p_D^{-1}\cong\bar x_D^{-1}$ naturally on $D(X_{\Et})$, with no boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor)(3)-(4), applied termwise to the composition isomorphism of topologies.tex Tag 021J; explicit chain-map naturality and localization argument

proof.text: Now let $\alpha:A\to B$ be a morphism in $D(X_{\Et})$ such that $p_D^{-1}\alpha$ is an isomorphism. Applying $\widetilde x_D^{-1}$ preserves its inverse, and the comparison of step 4 identifies the resulting morphism with $\bar x_D^{-1}\alpha$ up to conjugation by isomorphisms. Thus the pullback of $\alpha$ to every geometric point of $X$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-kun-stalk-faithful-derived] with $T=X$ to conclude that $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. The argument applies to the unbounded category, exactly as that cited statement does.

source.place: Proof, final parenthesis invoking lem-kun-stalk-faithful-derived; the needed unbounded composition comparison is supplied in step 4

proof.text: Conversely, in either category, if $\alpha$ has inverse $\beta$, functoriality gives $p^{-1}(\beta)p^{-1}(\alpha)=p^{-1}(\beta\alpha)=\mathrm{id}$ and $p^{-1}(\alpha)p^{-1}(\beta)=\mathrm{id}$ (and the same identities for $p_D^{-1}$). Thus pullback preserves isomorphisms. Together with steps 3 and 5 this proves both equivalences in the statement.
